records.title: STRATEGY FOR CLEANSING RECLEANSING THE RIVERS .
details:
(a) whether Government have devised any fresh strategy to cleanse/recleanse the rivers of, the country in the light of the experience gained in this regard from the earlier programmes/projects; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINIS`TRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)
(a) to (b) The objective of the National River Conservation Plan is to improve the water quality of the rivers through the implementation of the pollution abatement works like Interception and diversion works, Sewage treatment plants, low cost sanitation works, Electric crematoria and improved wood crematoria, River front development etc. In the light of the experience gained from these programs, Govt. has discussed fre`sh strategies with the State Governments for cleaning rivers in various fora. Among the points delibentted are: ,
o Urban local bodies/States laave the responsibility to create urban infrastructure so as to
ensure that untreated sewa~,e is not discharged into rivers and lakes.
o Additional resources may be generated for creation of such urban infrastructure by building into the external developmental costs, the cost of collection of sewage, its conveyance, treatment etc. wherever new urban centres are developed and such costs should be built into the price of developed land.
o States may also consider exploring other means for raising resources for capital
expenditure, such as, surcharge on property tax, stamp duty etc.
o Urban local bodies/State Governments need to further consider innovative ways for raising
revenue for meeting the ,operation and maintenance costs by adopting measures, such as,
 Levying user charges
 Sale of sludge
 Generation of power froth bio-gas in sewage treatment plants
 Creation of facilities for tourism
o Public participation and awareness t~rogrammes to generate awareness among the public for keeping water bodies clean, need to be also conducted simultaneously during implementation of pollution abatement schemes.

course; and
(d) the reasons that this benefit is not given to all consumers alike instead of choosing 
groups or sections of community which are considered vote banks by the political party in 
power in a State?

THE MINISTER OF POWER 
( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )
(a) &(b) : At present three States viz. Andhra Pradesh, Punjab and Tamil Nadu are giving 
free supply of power without any ceiling on consumption to certain categories of consumers like 
agriculture.
 In some other States, free supply of electricity is available to certain category of consumers only upto a very limited level of consumption or connected load.
 A statement indicating the States and expenditure involved on free supply of 
electricity as per available information is at annexure.
(c) & (d) : Under section 65 of the Electricity Act, 2003 , the State Government may grant 
subsidy from its budget to any class of consumers if it so desires in the tariff determined by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission. 
 The National Electricity Policy lays emphasis on ensuring recovery of cost of 
service from the consumers to make the power sector sustainable. The policy also provides that 
a minimum level of support may be required to consumers living below poverty line and 
consuming only up a specified level say 30 units/month. Tariff for such consumers should also be 
at least 50% of the cost of the average cost of supply.

records.title: SPECIAL CELL FOR SECURING RELEASE OF POWS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that family members of 54 soldiers believed to be in Pakistan 
jails since the 1965 and 1971 wars have demanded that Government set up a special cell
 to work on bringing them back; and
(b) the action Government have taken in the matter?

MINISTER OF DEFENCE 
(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)
(a) & (b): The Government have been taking up the matter of the release of Indian Prisoners of Wars with Pakistan through diplomatic channels and during high level visits from time to time. The matter was taken up by our Prime Minister with the Pakistan Prime Minister during the latter’s visit to Delhi from November 23-24, 2004 and also during the visit of President Musharraf to India from April 16-18, 2005. However, Pakistan has never acknowledged the presence of any Indian Prisoners of Wars in its jails.
In pursuance of the efforts of locating Indian Prisoners of Wars, the Government took up the matter with Pakistan Government for sending a delegation of the families of the missing defence personnel on a visit to various jails in Pakistan to facilitate identification of Indian Prisoners of War but this has not been accepted by Pakistan. A similar delegation had visited Pakistan in September, 1983 but it was given limited access and could not locate any Indian Prisoners of War.
Various proposals including setting up of a special cell to look into the matters of Prisoners of Wars in Pakistan have been received, but would be useful only if Pakistan agrees to engage in further discussions on the issue.

records.title: CHEQUE BOUNCE CASES IN I ELHI ANI MUMBAI .
details:
(a) what is the number of cheque bounce cases pending :in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and
Chennai at present under the National Instruments Act;
(b) whether the huge pendency is causing considerable ,delay in the disposal of these
cases; and
(c) the steps Government are contemplating m check the huge pendency?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALALANIMANICKAM)
a) Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 empowers the payee of the cheque to file a complaint under Section 141 of the Act against the drawer of the cheque in cases where cheques are dishonored for insufficient funds. As such it is left to the concerned parties to decide whether to approach the courts or not. The data base of Reserve Bank of India, therefore, does not generate information regarding cases pending in various courts relating to bouncing of cheques under th Negotiable Instrument Act. However, based ont he information received from Public Sector Banks, there are at present about 3024 cheque bounce cases pending in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai;
(b)&(c): Yes, Sir. In order to reduce pendency, the Negotiable Instalments Act was amended in December, 2002 and a new Section 143, was inserted providing for summery trial of` cases under the Act. The Section also provides that every endeavour shall be made by the Court to conclude the trial within six month:! of :filing the cornplaint.

records.title: RISE IN SENSEX .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)
(a): The stock markets have shown an upward trend over the last one year. On 1st December, 2004 the Sensex closed at 6227.83. It crossed 7000 to close at 7076.52 on 21st June 2005. It further rose to 7669.45 on l~t August, 2005. On 3rd October, 2005, it touched 8697.65 and closed at a new high 28th of 8994.94 on November, 2005. The closing figure for 1st December 2005 was 8944.78.
(b), (c) & (d) The movement of the index is a function of changes in investment arising out of perceptions about the economy and/or a sector or the stocks constituting the index. Besides economic factors, movement of stock indices also depends on various domestic and international events, market sentiments and corporate performance and likely economic growth in future, including the fundamentals of the economy. While there is no exact correlation between any of these factors and upward movement of the Sensex, a healthy growth in capital market is generally associated with increased investment in the economy including by foreign investors.
(e): The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the market regulator, keeps a constant vigil on the markets. In view of recent market movements, SEBI has taken several measures as a part of its surveillance activities. These include, inter alia, shifting of several scrips to trade-to-trade segment to discourage day trading and speculation and imposition of circuit filters/price bands on several scrips. SEBI has advised stock exchanges to initiate expeditious demonstrative action wherever warranted so as to protect investors` interests and to ensure orderly functioning of the stock market. Additionally, from time to time, stock exchanges issue lists of do`s ~and dont`s for investors with regard to dealing in securities, through leading English and Hindi newspapers. SEBI also emphasizes this through its periodic investor education programmes and encourages investors to take informed decisions. According to SEBI, these initiatives have minimized untoward speculation in small stocks.

records.title: DEPUTATION OF OFFICERS
details:

(b) whether it is a fact that the system promotes heart burning and is capable of lowering the productivity of officers belonging to regular establishment; and 
(c) if the reply to 
(a) above be in the negative, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.(SHRI SURESH PACHOURI)
(a) & (b): No, Sir. 
(c): Deputation enables Government, Public Sector Undertakings and other Organisations to 
obtain and benefit from the services of experienced officers, experts and professionals. Deputations also help organizations get over their manpower requirement especially when there 
is no feeder grade in a cadre or the strength of the feeder grade is not sufficient to sustain 100% promotion. Besides, in the case of isolated posts/posts created for temporary periods/
posts in temporary organizations, deputation is the most appropriate method of recruitment. Deputation also helps infuse fresh blood and talent into a cadre/organization. Often, the Recruitment Rules of such organizations or Government Departments provide for a complement of deputation as one of the modes of recruitment on terms which may vary from fixed term deputation to permanent absorption.

records.title: SCARCITY OF DRINKING WATER IN GUJARAT .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute crisis in North and Central Gujarat and 
 several districts of Saurashtra because of scarcity for drinking water; and
(b) what steps have been taken by Government to address the situation?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI A. NARENDRA)
(a) Based on the Comprehensive Action Plan, 1999 and the subsequent coverage 
reported by the Government of Gujarat, out of the 30,269 rural habitations in the State, 
30,233 have been fully covered with drinking water supply schemes to provide 40 litre 
per capita per day (lpcd), and the remaining 36 habitations partially covered to provide 
10-40 lpcd drinking water supply. However, the coverage position is dynamic and due to 
erratic rainfalls, some parts of the State face scarcity of drinking water, particularly 
during summer season. Based on the detailed assessment of the rainfall and its impact on 
drinking water supply, Government of Gujarat has notified 626 villages in 8 talukas of 
Kutch, Banaskantha and Sabarkantha districts as semi-scarcity affected villages. 
(b) Government of Gujarat has prepared a Master Plan for taking measures like 
drilling and developing additional tube-wells, rejuvenation of existing water supply 
schemes and supply of drinking water through tankers to tackle drinking water scarcity. 
Though drinking water is a State subject, the Central Government is rendering financial 
and technical support to the State Governments, including Government of Gujarat, under 
a Centrally sponsored scheme, namely Accelerated Rural Water Supply Programme 
(ARWSP). Funds allocated to the Government of Gujarat under different components of 
ARWSP during the current year (2005-2006) are as under: -
ARWSP (Normal) Rs.111.86 crore
ARWSP (DDP) Rs. 11.53 crore
ARWSP (Swajaldhara) Rs. 16.29 crore

records.title: LOSS DUE TO FLOODS IN H.P. .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that parts of Himachal Pradesh were flooded recently following 
 increase in the level of water in the Parchoo river;
(b) if so, the extent of losses caused by these floods and the steps taken to help the
 State; and
(c) what is the current status of the Parchoo river?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI S. REGUPATHY)
(a): Some parts of the State of Himachal Pradesh were affected by flash floods caused
due to heavy rains and breaches in the artificial lake formed by landslides on the river Parechu.
(b): In the first Memorandum submitted by the Government of Himachal Pradesh, in the wake
of these flash floods in June 2005, the estimated damage was reported at approximately
Rs. 610 crore. Thereafter, in the second Memorandum submitted by the State Government
which covers damage caused due to heavy rains and floods in some parts of the State in 
July 2005, was estimated at Rs. 398 crore.
 The Central Government extended timely required logistic and financial support
to the State Government to meet the situation. The logistic support extended to the 
State by the government of India included the deployment of manpower and air support to supplement the efforts of the State Government in rescue and relief operations and also 
for the restoration of connectively with the affected areas.
 The Government of India has released both the installments of Central share of 
Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) aggregating to an amount of Rs. 75.52 crore for the year 
2005-06 and an ad hoc release of Rs. 100 crore from National Calamity Contingency Fund 
(NCCF). An Inter Ministerial Central Team has visited the flood affected areas of the 
State on two occasions to asses the damage and requirement of funds for relief operations
by the State Government. The report of the Central Team, for providing additional 
assistance, is considered as per the extant norms and laid down procedure.
(c): As per available information, the artificial lake formed due to landslides on the 
river Parechu has broken down and at this stage, it does not pose any major potential 
threat to the downstream areas of Parechu river.

records.title: REDUCING DRUG PRICES.
details:
(a) whether Government are considering a proposal to reduce prices
 of life saving drugs and pain killers; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS & MINISTER OF STEEL( SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN )
(a) to (b): The Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO,95) does not make 
any distinction between Life Saving drugs and other drugs. There is no specific 
norms or guidelines to determine as to which drugs can be classified as life saving
drugs. Every drug, in general, is considered useful in saving and prolonging of life.
 Presently 74 bulk drugs specified in the First Schedule of the Drugs 
(Prices Control) Order, 1995 (DPCO, 95) and the formulations based thereon are 
under price control and their prices are fixed/revised by the National 
Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) in accordance with the provisions of 
the DPCO, 95. These drugs have been identified for inclusion under price control 
in the DPCO, 95 on the basis of criteria mentioned in the ‘Modifications in Drug 
Policy, 1986’, announced in September, 1994. These criteria take into account 
the extent of usage and the market competition in various drugs. 
Prices of non-Scheduled formulations are fixed by the manufacturers themselves
keeping in view the various factors like cost of production, marketing/selling 
expenses, R&D expenses, trade commission, market competition, product innovation,
product quality etc. Due to these factors there is a wide variation between the 
production cost and selling price of these medicines. The Government takes 
corrective measures where the public interest is found to be adversely affected.

(b):- In terms of the Reserve Bank directives and guidelines currency chest branches are required to verify, to process and to sort all the banknotes received by them both directly and from other branches and ensure that (a) banknotes unfit for further circulation are returned to the Reserve Bank and 
(b) good quality banknotes are reissued.
(c):- RBI has created public awareness to insist on issue of clean banknotes by the banks. Banks are also authorised to accept and exchange soiled, mutilated, etc., banknotes. Reserve Bank has directed that the currency chest branches are equipped with appropriate machines to expedite the process of verification, processing and sorting of banknotes. While some banks have already installed such machines, banks with more than 100 currency chests have been given time upto November 30, 2005, to install the machines.

records.title: REDUCTION IN FARES IN GULF SECTOR .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a record
 reduction in the fares to and fro Gulf countries by Air
 India, Indian Airlines and other carriers;
(b) if so, how this has been made possible despite the
 rising cost of fuel; and
(c) what has been its impact on passenger traffic?

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL
 AVIATION ( SHRI PRAFUL PATEL ) 
 (a),(b)&(c):- The airlines engaged in international air
 services to/from India are not required to file the fares
 with the Government and Government does not maintain details

 Airlines, there is no reduction in the IATA or Published

 these sectors.

records.title: ACUTE SHORTAGE OF DRINKING WATER AT RAILWAY STATIONS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an acute shortage of drinking water at various
 railway stations being faced by 98 per cent of the passengers; and
(b) the steps Government have taken to address the situation?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
(SHRI R. VELU)
(a) & (b) Indian Railways have more than 8000 stations. Railways endeavour is to provide drinking water to passengers at all stations. Some small stations do not have adequate water source either due to absence of water supply from municipality or presence of brackish water, inadequate ground water yield from hand pumps. Further, even at some of those stations where piped/hand pump supply exists, water scarcity comes up in summer due to lesser supplies by municipality, lowering in ground water table etc. and increased demand. In such cases, availability of drinking water is ensured at stations by arranging water through private water tankers. Even water special trains are run in areas facing heavy shortage of water. Water coolers, mobile water trollies, matkas are arranged for better availability of water to the passengers. Many Non Government Organisations also supplement water supply to passengers. In addition, packaged drinking water/natural mineral water is made available for sale through 
static as well as mobile catering/vending units.

records.title: STEM CELL RESEARCH .
details:
(a) whether Government have examined the possibility of the country becoming a nucleus
 of stem cell research; and

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER
OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT
(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)
(a) & (b) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.177 TO BE ANSWERED ON 04/08/2005 REGARDING STEM CELL RESEARCH
(a) Yes Madam. Brainstorming meetings on stem cells were organized to identify priorities 
and to examine the possibilities to enhance research in this area in the country. The main features of strategy include promotion of stem cell research for therapeutic applications 
using adult and embryonic stem cells as well as other more readily available sources such 
as bone marrow, peripheral blood and umbilical cord blood cells.
(b) Major initiatives have been taken to develop stem cell research programmes for limbal, haematopoitic, neural, liver, cardiac, embryonic and human corneal stem cells and the stem 
cell preservation. Limbal stem cells are being used at L.V. Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI), Hyderabad to repair cornea surface disorders caused by limbal stem cells deficiencies. Under
the programme supported at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, a technology has been established for collection, purification and haplo-identical haematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The studies conducted at the National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune
and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc.), Bangalore showed that banana lectins have stem
cell preservation activities. Long and short term training programme have been initiated. National and International conferences on the various aspects of the subject are being periodically organized. Inter institutional city clusters programmes have been implemented
at Vellore and Pune by involving basic researchers, clinicians and industry. This includes sharing of information, exploration of collaboration and discussion on emerging policy issues 
etc. Bangalore, Hyderabad and Delhi city cluster programmes are being considered. It is also proposed to establish Centres of Excellence
for stem cell research initially at 2 or 3 places to initiate focused, targeted programmes
on human stem cell research by involving basc researchers and clinicians. An advertisement
to invite proposals o identifiy sdathe programmes and the sites has been widely publicized.

records.title: CONTROL OF INTERNET
details:
:-
(a) whether it is a fact that currently the power to govern the
 internet rests with the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names
 and Numbers (ICANN), based in California;
(b) whether Government are contemplating to wrest control of
 internet on expiry of MoU in September, 2006 between ICANN and the
 Department of Commerce of the USA; and
(c) if so, the details in this regard?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY(DR.
SHAKEEL AHMAD)
(a): ICANN is an internationally organized, non-profit
corporation that has responsibility for Internet Protocol (IP)
address space allocation, protocol identifier assignment, generic 
(gTLD ) and country code (ccTLD) Top-Level Domain name system
management, and root server system management functions. As a
public-private partnership, ICANN is dedicated to preserving the
operational stability and security of the Internet.
(b) and (c): No Sir, Government after consultation with all
stakeholders have declared that governments and all stakeholders
should have effective say in all deliberations on Internet policy.
These should be transparent, inclusive and democratic.

records.title: SELF SUFFICIENCY BY INDIAN ARMED FORCES .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that on the occasion of celebration of Taknik
Diwas by Defence Research and Development Organisation Prime Minister
is reported to have stated that the Indian Armed Forces will have to
attain self-sufficiency;
(b) what is the current status of the Indian Armed Forces vis a vis
self-sufficiency; and
(c) whether the goal can be achieved in a time-frame?

MINISTER OF DEFENCE 
(SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE)
(a) Yes, Sir. Prime Minister stated that self-reliant military is
essential for our strategic autonomy.
(b) Government has the policy of progressively enhancing indigenous
content of weapon systems in the Armed Forces. We are self reliant
in several areas of military technology i.e. arms & ammunition,
combat and armoured vehicles, guided missiles, aircraft,
communication, radars and sonar systems.
(c) Self-sufficiency is dictated by threat perception in a region
which is a continuously changing phenomenon. India is moving
steadily in the direction of achieving the goal of self-sufficiency.

records.title: WATER CRISIS IN RAJASTHAN .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rajasthan seems to set for a spell
 of water crisis and consequently the riots; and
(b) the steps Government have taken to address the situation?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV)
(a) As per Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) that regulates
Sutlej and Ravi-Beas waters, the position of water availability
in BBMB’s reservoirs, due to the normal monsoon this year so far,
is very comfortable and has enabled BBMB to meet the full water
requirements of the Partner States including Rajasthan. Further,
BBMB has delivered an average of 13,488 cusecs to Rajasthan from
1st to 28th July, 2005 against Rajasthan’s share of 13,025 cusecs
and BBMB has even requested the Partner States to maximize their
drawals notwithstanding their respective shares so as to avoid
the wastage of water downstream of Madhopur and Ferozepur
Headworks.
Water availability in important reservoirs monitored Central
Water Commission has also indicated that the aggregate current
year’s storage as on 22.7.05 in Mahi Bajaj Sagar, Jhakam and Rana
Pratap Sagar reservoirs in Rajasthan is about 1.45 thousand
million cubic metres, which is 240% of the last year’s storage
and 197% of the last 10 year’s average storage during the
corresponding period.
(b) Handing over of successful exploratory wells by Central
Ground Water Board (CGWB) to the Rajasthan State Government and
technical assistance from CGWB to the State for promotion of rain
water harvesting and artificial recharge of ground water etc. are
some of the on-going steps and will be of help in a crisis
situation.

records.title: SELF SUFFICIENCY IN OIL SECTOR .
details: MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)

(a): whether it is a fact that the country is running out of oil with 0.4 per cent of 
the world’s oil reserves left in the country for 15 per cent of the world’s population; 
(b): what is the status of the oil reserves of other countries vis a vis their population; 
(c): whether the self-sufficiency in oil has now become a distant dream, 
if so, what is the annual production in the country at present and projections for 
the next five years; and(d): the steps Government are contemplating to address the 
situation? 
(a) & (b): As on 1.4.2005, proven oil reserves in the country are to 
the order of 740 Million Metric Tonnes(MMT), which are about 0.5% of the total proven 
reserves of the world. India has about 28 billion tonnes of prognosticated hydrocarbon
reserves, out of which, only 8.2 billion tonnes of hydrocarbon reserves have been 
established so far. The status of oil reserves vis-à-vis population is annexed 
(source:B.P statistics) 
(c): Given the present demand scenario and the status of 
production of oil in the country, self-sufficiency is not envisaged in the near future. 
The production of crude oil for the year 2004-05 was 33.980 MMT. 
According to current estimates the projections of crude oil production for the next 5
years are as follow:-
(figures in MMT) 2005-06 2006-07 2007-08 2008-09 2009-10 
 34.67 35.90 39.62 37.26 37.07 
(d): The following steps have already
been taken to enhance oil security:- 
(i) Accelerating domestic hydrocarbon exploration. 
(ii) Implementation of Improved Oil Recovery(IOR)/Enhanced Oil Recovery(EOR) projects to
enhance oil recovery. 
(iii) Offer new acreages through New Exploration Licensing 
Policy(NELP). Already 108 exploration blocks have been awarded including 18 exploration 
blocks offered under fifth round of NELP. 
(iv) Acquisition of overseas oil and gas assets. 
(v) Development of alternate sources such as Coal Bed Methane(CBM), Underground Coal 
Gassification(UCG) and Gas Hydrates. 
(vi) Storage of oil. 
(vii) Conservation of oil.

 market from 1993 to 1995 have disappeared with a sum of about Rs.1700 crores;

MINISTER OF COMPANY AFFAIRS 
( SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA)
(a) 71 companies stand identified as on date as Vanishing Companies which came out with IPOs during the period 1993-1995, for raising a sum of Rs.607.65 crores from the public.

records.title: ARRANGEMENTS FOR COMMONWEALTH GAMES .
details:
(a) whether Government have reviewed the arrangements in connection with Commonwealth
Games 2010; if so, with what results;
(b) whether it is a fact that distractions near the Games Village including railway track
 and Akshardham Temple, traffic bottlenecks and venues being located far away from city`s 
airports are some of the problems; and 
(c) the steps contemplated to address the situation?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN)
(a) Government of India has constituted a Core Group of Ministers (GOM) for coordinating
the work relating to the organization of the Commonwealth Games, 2010. An Apex Committee for
overseeing and coordinating the Games has been set up. An Organizing Committee under the 
Chairmanship of President, IOA for conduct of the Games has been constituted.
The arrangements for holding the Commonwealth Games 2010 at Delhi are underway. A review of existing infrastructure in the city of Delhi in context of Commonwealth Games 2010 has been undertaken. The existing infrastructure with Sports Authority of India (SAI), Delhi 
Development Authority (DDA) and New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC) with required upgradation and renovation would be used for most of the disciplines covered under the Commonwealth Games. 
A Task Force for upgradation/renovation of SAI`s infrastructure has been set up and the consultancy on SAI`s existing infrastructure has been assigned to CPWD. Condition Survey of
SAI`s existing five Stadia at Delhi has been undertaken. 
Regarding construction of a Commonwealth Games Village, a site off the Nizamuddin Bridge 
has been identified. Delhi Development Authority has also commenced the action to prepare preliminary designs in respect of new venues & Games Village proposed to be constructed by
it. 
A core Committee has been set up by Government of NCT of Delhi under the Chairmanship of
Chief Secretary, Delhi to prepare a master plan for improvement/up gradation of civic 
amenities in Delhi for Commonwealth Games, 2010. The Government of NCT of Delhi is in the
process of finalizing plans for up gradation of roads, health care, civic amenities, 
traffic management and parking for the Commonwealth Games.
(b) DDA have engaged M/s Event Knowledge Service for Venue Reappraisal Study who 
have submitted a draft report. The draft report has flagged issues like traffic 
bottlenecks, proximity to Akshardham Tample & a railway track, distance from airport,
etc.
( c) The matter is being discussed with various stakeholders to meet these concerns.

the festivities, birthday parties and dance shows than the
bonafide purposes for which it is meant as reported in the media
recently;
(b) if so, what are the reasons therefor; and

used for bonafide purposes only?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI M.A.A. FATMI)
(a), (b) & (c): According to the information furnished by the
University of Delhi, consequent upon appearance of certain
allegations about the misuse of Gandhi Bhawan in a section of the
Press, a Fact Finding Committee was constituted by the
University. The report of this Committee has revealed that one of

future. These include repatriation of an official working in the
Bhawan on deputation basis; issue of warning letter to another
official for his administrative lapses; expression of displeasure
of the Vice- Chancellor to the concerned Professor; and issue of
directions to enforce stringent guidelines for the management of
the affairs of the Gandhi Bhawan in strict accordance with the
resolution of the Executive Council.

records.title: REVIVAL OF MALARIA .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a): The mosquito nuisance is determined by several factors like unplanned urbanization, physical environment, life style of the people and water-management system. There are several species of the mosquitos which have different breeding habits. The mosquito for spread of malaria i.e. `Anopheles` usually breeds in clean water. The effective control of mosquito can be achieved by environmental modifications & manipulations. The National Malaria Control Programme was started by the Govt.of India in 1953 which was converted to National Malaria Eradication Programme in 1958. There was spectacular reduction of malaria incidence as well as deaths. However, during late 1970`s there was resurgence of malaria due to operational, technical and administrative factors. With the introduction of Modified Plan of Operation in 1977, the number of malaria cases declined from 6.4 million to below 2 million in 2002. Since then the number of cases of malaria has remained below 2 million.
(b): Though there are some reports in literature about the insecticidal and repellent activity of the extracts of Tagetus (Marigold), these have not been used/studied as malaria repellent by planting of Marigold flowers and other plants in the country.
 There is however a report on a study conducted by scientists from Kenya and Ethiopia on live potted plants including Tagetus (Marigold) tested as mosquito repellent which did not show any significant repellent effect of Tagetus.
(c) & (d): Bad sewerage system cause breeding of Culex mosquitos but malaria transmitting Anopheles mosquitos do not breed in sewer water.
 The Govt.of India has a well defined Programme viz. National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme(NVBDCP) for control of malaria in the country adopting strategies which include surveillance, early diagnosis and prompt treatment of cases, sustainable vector control including Indoor Residual Spray with insecticides treated bednets, use of larvivorous fish etc. besides Training & Information, Education and Communication to enlist community involvement. Urban Malaria Scheme is also being implemented in 131 Towns in the country to reduce density of mosquitoes and to prevent spread of malaria.

(b) whether it is also a fact that a considerable amount out of the funds earmarked 
towards the physically challenged remained unutilized; 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(SMT. MEIRA KUMAR)
(a) to (d) A statement is laid on the table of the House. 
Statement referred to in the reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 358 
put forth by Shrimati Jaya Bachchan, regarding Non-utilisation of funds 
earmarked for physically challenged for answer on 18.4.2005.
(a) No report from the National Centre for Promotion of Employment for the 
Disabled People has been received by this Ministry. 
(b) to (d) No, Sir. The utilization of funds is measured as difference in Revised 
Estimates and actual expenditure. Thus, the unspent amount for disability sector 
for the IX Plan was Rs.35.07 crores as against the revised estimate of Rs.790.03 
crores. Major reasons for non-utilisation of funds were:
1) State Governments took time to formulate projects and set up mechanism 
for implementation.
2) The office of Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (CCD) 
could be set up only by the middle of the 9th Plan due to administrative 
procedure involved in getting required clearances/ approvals.
The total Plan outlay for the 10th Plan is Rs.1454.10 crores. During the 10th Five 
Year Plan, for the year 2002-03, expenditure was Rs.194.05 crores against the 
Revised Estimate (RE) of Rs.192.37 crore. Thus, there was slight excess 
expenditure. For the Year 2003-2004, the expenditure was Rs.168.92 crores 
against an RE of Rs.186.25 crores. Thus, there was a shortfall of Rs.17.33 
crores. The shortfall was on account of delays in receipt of utilization certificates 
from the NGOs and the recommendation of State Governments as well as time 
taken in completing procedural formalities under certain schemes. For the year 
2004-05, the expenditure (provisional)was Rs.175.54 crores against an RE of

records.title: PERFORMANCE OF KISAN CREDIT CARD SCHEME QUESTION .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THF, MINISTRY OF FINANCE
 (SHRI S.S.PALANIMANICKAM)
(a) Kisan Credit Card(KCC) Scheme has emerged as a widely accepted mechanism for delivery of hassle-free crop loan to farmers. The scheme, introduced in August 1998 as an innovative credit delivery mechanism, has been progressing satisfactorily. About 4.80 crore KCCs have been issued till 31st January, 2005. The scope of the scheme has been recently enlarged to cover the term loans for agriculture and allied activities including a reasonable component to meet consumption needs besides the existing facility of providing crop loan limit. 
(b): No ceiling has been envisaged for sanction of credit limit under the scheme. However, the banks may fix the credit limit to farmers on the basis of their land holding, cropping pattern and scale of finance recommended by the District Level Technical Committee. The Co-operative Banks also take into account the individual maximum borrowing power fixed by the Registrar of the Co-operative Societies while fixing the credit limit under the scheme which may vary from State to State. As the interest rate regime has been deregulated by the Reserve Bank of India, banks have been provided freedom to fix the rate of interest on credit limit sanctioned. Hence, no uniform rate of interest is applicable to KCC in respect of Co-operative Banks and regional Rural Banks. However, Commercial Banks cannot charge interest rate exceeding their Benchmark Prime Lending Rate(BPI-,II) for the loans up to Rs. 2.00 lakh. 
(c) and (d): The scheme is applicable all over the country.

Municipal Corporation, Delhi Cantonment Board, Delhi State Industrial Development Corporation 
and Government of Uttar Pradesh for preparation of an integrated action plan for cleaning of 
river Yamuna. The action plan has already been drawn up based on the inputs provided by all 
the agencies concerned to address various contributory factors leading to the pollution in 
Yamuna. The action plan includes augmentation in the capacity of sewage treatment plants, 
rehabilitation of trunk sewers, management of waste water in the Najafgarh drain, Shahdara 
drain and other drains, laying of sewer lines in the unsewered areas of Delhi, resettlement/
clearance of slum clusters on the Yamuna river bank/bed, treatment of industrial effluents, 
utilization of treated effluent and removal of coliform at sewage treatment plants.

records.title: AMERICAN AID TO SILL LANKA FOR TSUNAMI RELIEF
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI E. AHAMED)
(a), (b) & (c) According to figures released by the US Embassy in Colombo a total of about 830 US Armed Forces personnel were deployed on the ground in Sri Lanka. This included about 700 US Marines. This excludes US personnel manning ships deployed off the coast of Sri Lanka who would probably have numbered between 700 to 900.
The tsunami disaster in Sri Lanka and other Indian Ocean rim countries attracted a very high degree of international attention mad evoked an enormous outpouring of compassion and international assistance to the affected countries, including Sri Lanka. The scale of the devastation caused was so great that all relief contributions were welcome. India was a key player in this major international humanitarian effort in Sri Lanka and other affected countries and was, along with the United States, a member of` the Core Group that coordinated relief in the initial phases.
The Indian Navy launched ``Operation Rainbow` the day the tsunami struck. The first Indian naval Dornier carrying 650kg of medical supplies and a medical team arrived in Sri Lanka on December 26 itself Almost simultaneously, four Indian naval ships steamed towards the ports of Galle and Trincomalee. These vessels, which picked up relief supplies on the way, reached Sri Lanka just over 24 hours afterwards and immediately commenced relief and damage control operations. Tiffs deployment was stepped up to include stationing of an air detachment of ten aircraft for three weeks, about fifteen naval ship-loads of supplies, fifteen medical teams including a mobile field hospital (140 men) that was airlifted and specialist doctors, a 45-bed hospital ship (INS Jamuna) that was anchored of Galle and Trincomalee for two weeks, ten teams of naval divers mad a 8 I-member. composite Army disaster management team.
Sri Lankan President Kumaratunga, Prime Minister Rajapakse and several Sri Lankan Ministers have expressed the gratitude of the people of Sri Laaaka for Indian assistance. President Kumaratunga also dispatched Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar as Special Envoy to thank India for its generous contribution to the relief efforts.

details:

(a) &(b): As per information available with the Ministry, for

out rate are:

to 14 years.
- Monitoring of attendance by the community.
- Micro planning and household survey to identify the
dropouts and reasons therefor.

increasing enrolment, retention and attendance and
simultaneously impacting on the nutrition of students in
primary classes.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)
(a): No, Sir.
, 
(b): To ensure safety of internet transactions, the Reserve Bank of India has issued guidelines on Internet Banking in India to all Scheduled Commercial Banks. The guidelines were based on the recommendations of the `Working Group on Internet Banking set up by the Reserve Bank of India to examine the different aspects of Internet Banking. The guidelines, which were issued for implementation by banks, focus on Security and Technology standards, apart from dealing regulatory and Supervisory issues as well as Legal. issues pertaining to Internet Banking. All banks offering Internet Banking services are required to strictly adhere to the Security and Technology Standards prescribed in the guidelines. Their compliance with the standards is also checked in course of the annual financial inspection of the banks carried out
by the Reserve Bank of India.

records.title: LIMIT TO CROSS SHARE HOLDING OF BANKS .
details:
(a) whether Government have decided to tighten the cross share holding roles of the entire

(€) if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM)
(a) & (b) Reserve Bank of India monitors cross holding of capital among banks and 
financial institutions. A bank`s aggregate investment in Tier II Bonds issued by other 
banks and financial institutions is permitted upto I0 percent of the investing bank`s 
capital funds. They also should not acquire any fresh stake in a bank`s equity shares if 
by such acquisition the investing banks/FIs holding exceeds 5 percent of the investee bank`s 
equity capital. The above ceiling are applicable to all types of instrument listed below which 
are issued by other banks/FIs and are eligible for capital status for the investee bank/FIs:-
(i) Equity shares
(ii) Preference shares eligible for capital status;
(iii) Subordinate debt instruments;
(iv) Hybrid debt capital instruments, and
(v) Any other instrument approved as in the nature of capital
(c) Does not arise.
